item.title: Getting started with Speedle Cloud
item.description: Speedle Cloud is coming soon. This guide describes the workflow available when production sign-in and authenticated authorization checks open; the examples have not been run against a live Cloud environment. Sign in with GitHub or Google (opens soon) Open the Cloud console in your browser and sign in with an available provider. For a new identity with an unused verified email address, confirm Create account. If the email is already in use, sign in with the linked provider shown by the console.

item.title: Speedle Cloud application tokens
item.description: Application tokens authenticate an application to Speedle Cloud ADS for the token’s own service. They do not identify an end user and cannot authorize management API requests. The token console becomes available when account sign-in opens; while authenticated ADS is pending, issuing a token does not enable server-side authorization calls. Issue a token For an account that already owns a service, open Application tokens. Enter a token name of 1–128 characters and choose Create token.

item.title: Speedle Cloud limits and errors
item.description: The ADS errors and headers below describe the authenticated ADS contract, whose runtime is not yet available. The management contract already defines account limits, session and CSRF checks, and token-management errors for use when account access is available. Downloading a schema does not enable a pending endpoint. Limits Limit Meaning 10,000 calls per day Account-wide matched PMS and ADS handler calls per UTC day, across sessions, tokens and services; resets at 00:00 UTC.
